newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists to review Vilvorde if elected.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists to review Vilvorde if elected.

text.p: France's Socialists will review the planned closure of carmaker Renault SA's Belgian plant at Vilvorde if they win the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election, their leader Lionel Jospin said on Monday.
Former Socialist prime minister Pierre Mauroy, receiving a a delegation of protesting Vilvorde workers as the mayor of the northern French city of Lille, read them a letter from Jospin.

"In case of victory in the parliamentary election, we would ask to re-open the case to solve the problems, which would involve discussing industrial and social problems with trade unions," the letter said.

"State shareholders on the Renault board would demand that other measures be considered, studied and prepared to solve the difficulties that may exist regarding production costs at the Vilvorde plant," it said.

Jospin criticised in his letter the way Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer had dealt with the plant. Schweitzer announced last February he planned to shut down the Belgian plant on July 31 in a reorganisation of Renault's European network, threatening 3,100 jobs.
Work resumed at Vilvorde on April 14 after a six-week strike to protest against the factory closure which could be stopped by court orders.
